name: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis
summary: Narrowing of the spinal canal can cause leg pain or heaviness with walking that eases with sitting or bending forward; exercise, walking programmes, posture strategies and education help most patients, and surgery is reserved for severe or progressive cases.

looksLike: Walking tolerance and symptom behaviour (neurogenic claudication)
Relief with sitting or forward bending
redFlags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Progressive leg weakness or foot drop
Severe unremitting night pain or unexplained weight loss
firstSteps: Record walking time, symptom behaviour and the position that relieves it.
Screen the legs neurologically and check pulses if vascular claudication is possible.
Teach a short walking-and-rest strategy and a few starter exercises.
selfCare: Sit or lean forward to settle symptoms

assess: Walking tolerance and symptom behaviour (neurogenic claudication)

do: Walking in intervals and flexion-biased positions
dose: Interval walking: walk until symptoms start, rest in a flexed position, repeat, aiming for 20 to 30 minutes in total.
Stationary cycling: 15 to 30 minutes, 3 to 5 days a week.
Hip and trunk strengthening: 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 repetitions, 2 to 3 days a week.
Hamstring and hip flexor mobility: daily.

education: Explain that symptoms are related to posture and that bending forward often eases them.
Teach the warning signs of cauda equina syndrome.
Encourage daily activity and weight management if relevant.
escalation: Urgent assessment for bladder or bowel change, saddle numbness or rapid weakness
Specialist review if function remains poor after several months of good rehabilitation
